title: Empathic stress transmission and positive social affect training in major depression disorder
summary: A person's social environment plays a key role in the course of depressive disorders. Stress in the social environment, especially in the partnership, can have an unfavourable effect on the course of depressive symptoms. One possible factor influencing this process is empathic stress transfer, i.e. the development of individual stress symptoms through the observation of stress in others. Whether training programmes to promote social skills and positive feelings such as empathy can mitigate or even reverse partner stress transference has not yet been sufficiently investigated. In this sub-project of the Collaborative Research Centre "SFB/TRR 393 - Progression of Affective Disorders: Cognitive-emotional mechanisms of symptom modification", we want to find out whether the transmission of stress can be changed through targeted exercises in everyday life and whether this can prevent the development of depressive symptoms in the long term. We are investigating 100 people with a history of depression and their partners in comparison with the same number of healthy couples. Half of the participants receive an eight-week positive social affect training programme consisting of two structured exercises in everyday life. It includes compassion meditation and a structured couple's dialogue and lasts 30 minutes per day. The other half receive mindfulness training of the same scope as an active control group. We measure how this training affects the following areas over a period of 24 months: daily social interactions and stress, compassion and other social skills, transmission of negative feelings within the partnership and depressive symptoms. We use various methods such as interviews, brain scans (fMRI) and cortisol measurements. The results should show whether and how social stress transmission can be mitigated through training and not only alleviate symptoms, but also protect against depression in the long term. These findings could help to improve the treatment and support of people with affective disorders.

interventions.name:
experimental group:
The experimental group receives an eight-week positive social affect training programme consisting of two structured exercises in everyday life. It includes a compassion meditation and a structured couple dialogue, lasts 30 minutes per day and is carried out independently by the

active control group:
As an active control group, the control group receives mindfulness training of the same scope, which includes body scans and sessions on mindful breathing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Target subjects:
o    Aged 18–65 
o    BMI >17 and <30
o    In a stable heterosexual relationship for at least 6 months 
o    Partner willing to participate in the study 
o    Not pregnant/breastfeeding 
o    No illnesses/medication affecting the HPA axis or immune activity
o    No accompanying psychological treatment
o    Stable medication for >3 months
o    MDD group: History of MDD diagnosis, currently (partially) remitted 
o    HC group: No lifetime F diagnosis (exception: nicotine) 

Partners
•	Stable relationship with target for 6 months
•    Willingness to participate in study
•    Shared household for 6 months
•    No pregnancy/breastfeeding
•    No diseases/medication affecting the HPA axis or immune activity
•    BMI of >17 or <30
•    50%: SLE in last 12 months
Exclusion criteria:
o    MRI contraindications (metal implants, pacemakers, claustrophobia, pregnancy, etc.)
o    Shift work (decided on a case-by-case basis)
o    History of organic brain disorders (e.g., seizures, stroke, multiple sclerosis, dementia, Hashimoto's disease, lupus, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, type 1 diabetes, HIV, serum hepatitis C, Lyme disease)
o    History of serious medical conditions (e.g., cancer, autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammatory diseases)
